headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Kotaemon handles broad networked document ingestion while Great Expectations writes validation artifacts that can be reused as trusted inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation results and documentation to files, and Kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, and chat transcripts via a web UI. If GE outputs are placed in Kotaemon’s workspace, attacker-controlled content can be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is plausible from profiles alone, but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are copied into Kotaemon's indexed workspace
IF Kotaemon treats ingested document text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Separate the GE output directory from Kotaemon ingestion paths
Add a manual review step before indexing GE-generated files
Prefix GE outputs with non-executable metadata headers
Restrict Kotaemon collections to human-authored documents only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and has broad network egress. If both share a workspace or files are imported into Kotaemon, sensitive validation artifacts can be sent to third-party APIs. Because Kotaemon’s default API-backed workflow is exposed and the pairwise sharing path is plausible, high is warranted.
conditions: IF GE validation results contain sensitive source data
IF those files are opened or indexed by Kotaemon using a remote model backend
mitigations: Keep GE outputs out of ./ktem_app_data
Use a local-only model backend in Kotaemon
Redact secrets from validation artifacts before import
Disable automatic document ingestion for GE outputs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with separate containers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can write files for validation results and documentation, and Kotaemon supports multiple instances plus writes under ./ktem_app_data. If both operate on the same directory, concurrent writes can corrupt artifacts or overwrite outputs. The profiles do not prove a shared directory by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem directory
IF Kotaemon and Great Expectations write overlapping filenames or subpaths
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories per agent
Run only one writer per shared path at a time
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Snapshot the workspace before batch runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Kotaemon can ingest as documents and citations. If Kotaemon treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, a bad validation artifact can cascade into incorrect summaries or support responses. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Kotaemon uses GE validation outputs as source documents
IF downstream responses are generated without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before citing GE outputs
Mark GE artifacts as untrusted source material
Add a verification checklist for imported validation reports
Limit Kotaemon to retrieval-only mode for GE files
requires-engineering: add source-confidence scoring

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can send content to external APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is present, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through remote processing. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in GE validation artifacts
IF Kotaemon forwards those artifacts to a non-compliant external API
mitigations: Exclude regulated datasets from Kotaemon ingestion
Use a local model backend for sensitive collections
Set explicit retention limits for imported files
Review API-key handling before enabling remote connectors
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
